longterm_view.reasoning: Revenue is growing (15.9% two-year CAGR, 29.2% in the latest year; SaaS segment nearly doubled to ₹2,043 million) [business, page 228], but the company has burned operating cash in all three disclosed years — even though the burn is shrinking from ₹548 million to ₹18 million, I cannot tell from what I was given whether the latest year is genuine turn to self-funding or working-capital timing. With no ROE, ROCE, EPS or balance-sheet figures printed, there is no basis to say the business creates value, only that it is shrinking its losses.

governance.reasoning: The prospectus itself flags criminal proceedings against Promoters and Directors Kunal Bahl and Rohit Kumar Bansal [litigation, page 477], which is a first-order governance fact the seller chose to bury in a litigation chapter. Related-party claims of arm's-length dealing are standard self-assertions [promoters, page 370] and carry little weight without the underlying transaction detail.

Three consecutive years of operating cash burn mean the listing is, in substance, a refinancing of losses; the improving trend is one data point, not a track record.

answers.question: Our reading triggered a hard stop: negative operating cash flow in all three years. Is there an explanation in the document?
answers.answer: No direct explanation is in the extracts I was given. The circumstantial evidence is that the company runs an inventory-less marketplace and logistics model ('We do not own or store any inventory') with a fast-growing SaaS line, which is consistent with deliberate investment-heavy, working-capital-negative scaling rather than a broken core business — and the burn is improving sharply year over year. But 'consistent with' is not 'explained': nothing in the extracts states why cash flow is negative, and the document does not print ROE, ROCE or a cash-flow discussion I could check. Treat the hard stop as unresolved.

answer.what_would_change_my_mind: A clean explanation of the negative operating cash flow in the cash-flow chapter (e.g., deliberate SaaS/logistics capex or receivables build) plus confirmation that the latest year's near-breakeven is structural, and a corrected offer split showing the fresh issue genuinely funds the company rather than exiting holders.
